identity.title: Targeting cancer immune evasion with anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate potentiates anti-PD-1 efficacy in colorectal cancer.

content.abstract: Loss of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) antigen presentation in tumor cells drives immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in colorectal cancer (CRC). To identify therapeutic targets reversing this, we conducted fluorescence-activated cell sorting-based CRISPR activation screens using a druggable genome library and identified folate receptor alpha (FOLR1) as a top negative regulator. FOLR1 was heterogeneously expressed in CRC tumors but undetectable in adjacent normal tissues. High expression of FOLR1 predicted a poor ICB response, enhanced cancer stemness, and unfavorable patient outcomes. Functional assays showed that FOLR1 promoted CRC stemness-associated properties and fostered an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) with impaired CD8(+) T cell infiltration and cytotoxicity, thereby driving tumor progression. Proteomic analyses revealed that FOLR1 stabilized the lactyltransferase AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1), which lactylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) at lysine-193 (K193), facilitating its interaction with TCPTP (T cell protein-tyrosine phosphatase) and inducing STAT1 dephosphorylation at tyrosine-701. Consequently, impaired STAT1 signaling down-regulated MHC-I and up-regulated MYC proto-oncogene protein (c-MYC), facilitating evasion of T cell surveillance and enhancing cancer stemness. The anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) mirvetuximab soravtansine (IMGN853) exhibited potent activity against FOLR1-positive CRC cells, reprogramming the TME to an immune-active status. Combining IMGN853 with anti-PD-1 (programmed cell death protein-1) therapy boosted antitumor immunity, sensitized tumors to immunotherapy, and induced robust tumor regression in vivo. Our findings support anti-FOLR1 ADC as a clinically actionable approach to overcome immune evasion and unlock immunotherapy efficacy in CRC.
